title: Ask for the 15-min call directly
why_now_template: They replied. You are still chatting. Ask for the call now with a specific window.
done_looks_like: Call-booking message sent to every current replier.
deliverable_prompt: Draft the exact reply that transitions from chat to a 15-minute call, including 2 specific time windows.

title: Send a 3-bullet call agenda
why_now_template: People say no to open-ended calls. A tight agenda with what they get raises accept-rate.
done_looks_like: Agenda-forward call invite sent to each replier.
deliverable_prompt: Write a 3-bullet call agenda framed as what the prospect gets from the 15 minutes.

title: Write direct responses to the 3 objections you keep hearing
why_now_template: Same 3 objections mean the offer or positioning has a hole. Address them in writing and resend.
done_looks_like: One reply per objection, sent to every open prospect.
deliverable_prompt: Ask the founder for the 3 objections they hear most; draft direct, honest, non-defensive responses to each.

title: Cut scope, hold price — test lower-friction commitment
why_now_template: Persistent price resistance rarely means lower price. It usually means smaller first commitment. Test scope, not discount.
done_looks_like: A pilot version of the offer defined: 50-70% of the scope at 60-80% of the price, with a clear upgrade path back to the full engagement.
deliverable_prompt: Guide the founder to design a pilot version of their productized offer that reduces scope without dropping headline price to zero. Rules: (1) name the 1-2 deliverables kept and the 2-3 removed; (2) new price 60-80% of full price; (3) 2-4 week window; (4) explicit upgrade path back to full engagement with credit applied. Do not recommend a straight discount. Do not invent specific customer objection quotes.

title: Ask each lost prospect why — before diagnosing anything else
why_now_template: You cannot fix a pattern you cannot see. Structured loss reasons unlock every close-family intervention downstream.
done_looks_like: A short follow-up sent to every lost prospect from the last 30 days asking one question: what was the deciding factor.
deliverable_prompt: Write a 60-90 word follow-up message the founder can send to each lost prospect. One question only: what was the deciding factor in not moving forward, with 5 short options (price, unclear ROI, timing, trust/proof, poor fit) plus a free-text option. Do not invent prospect names or prior conversation details. Frame it as helping the founder improve, not re-selling. End with a note to log each response back into TrueBlazer so the diagnosis sharpens.

title: Build a one-pager showing what the offer changes in dollars
why_now_template: When "unclear ROI" is the dominant loss reason, the fix is a concrete, buyer-shaped economic case — not a price cut.
done_looks_like: A one-pager the founder can send with future proposals: before/after, quantified impact, timeframe, and one plausible outcome scenario.
deliverable_prompt: Produce the ONE-PAGER itself (not advice). Sections in this order: (1) 'The cost of not solving this' — 2-3 lines quantifying the current pain in the buyer's own units (time or dollars), stating each number as ⟨FOUNDER: assumption⟩ if not supplied; (2) 'What changes after this engagement' — 2-3 lines in the same units; (3) 'Payback' — one line, stated as an assumption tied to the founder's own numbers, NOT a benchmark like '90 days' or 'within the first quarter'; (4) 'Honest caveat' — one line naming what could make this not work. NEVER cite industry benchmarks, 'typical' payback windows, testimonials, or invented customer results.

title: Set a 30- and 60-day follow-up sequence for timing losses
why_now_template: When "timing" is the dominant loss reason, the deal is not dead — the calendar is wrong.
done_looks_like: A 30/60-day follow-up sequence scheduled for each timing-loss prospect with one value-add per touch.
deliverable_prompt: Write a 2-touch follow-up sequence (day 30, day 60) the founder can send to prospects who declined for timing reasons. Each touch: one specific value-add (a data point, a template, a short observation) tied to the buyer segment, and a soft re-open of the conversation. No hard sell in touch 1. Do not invent prior discussion details. 80-120 words per touch.

title: Pull 25 fits from your existing audience
why_now_template: You have an audience. Fits are already there — you just have not looked yet.
done_looks_like: 25 audience members who match the buyer segment.
deliverable_prompt: Guide the founder through filtering their existing audience (channel + size in context) for 25 buyer-fit names.

title: Build a list of 25 named buyers
why_now_template: You have a locked offer but zero named humans to sell to. 25 is the minimum for signal.
done_looks_like: 25 rows: name, company, channel, why-they-fit.
deliverable_prompt: Given the buyer_segment, describe how to find 25 named buyers in the next 60 minutes. Include 3 concrete search strings for LinkedIn / Twitter / communities.

title: Pull 10 warm-network buyers first
why_now_template: Warm buyers close 5-10x higher than cold. Exhaust the network before touching cold.
done_looks_like: 10 named people from your existing network who fit the buyer segment.
deliverable_prompt: Walk the founder through pulling 10 warm-network buyer candidates from LinkedIn 1st-degree, past clients, and their audience.

title: Define what is NOT included
why_now_template: Productized means fixed scope. Buyers will not commit to something with unclear boundaries.
done_looks_like: A bullet list: 3 things included, 3 things explicitly excluded.
deliverable_prompt: Draft the in-scope / out-of-scope bullets for this productized offer.

title: Name the offer
why_now_template: A named offer converts higher than "consulting." Name it now.
done_looks_like: A memorable 2-4 word name that describes the outcome.
deliverable_prompt: Generate 5 candidate names for this productized offer. Prioritize outcome-oriented, easy to say aloud, no jargon.

title: Set a defensible price anchor
why_now_template: Without a price you cannot test demand. Pick one now; you can change it after 5 real conversations.
done_looks_like: A single price + one sentence justifying it against buyer ROI.
deliverable_prompt: Propose a starting price for a productized service given the buyer segment and delivery scope. Justify with buyer ROI, not cost-plus.

title: Reframe as a paid pilot
why_now_template: Full offer too heavy. Pilot lowers the yes-threshold and gets you a paying customer this week.
done_looks_like: Pilot offer sent to warmest 2 prospects.
deliverable_prompt: Draft a paid pilot version of the offer: shorter timeline, ~1/3 price, defined success metric.

title: Send a 1-page written offer within 24h
why_now_template: Momentum dies fast after calls. One-page written offer, sent today, closes the loop.
done_looks_like: A one-page offer PDF/doc sent to every prospect you have called.
deliverable_prompt: Draft a 1-page written offer: outcome, scope, timeline, price, next step. Concrete, no fluff.

title: Write your one-line offer
why_now_template: You have no locked offer. Everything downstream stalls until a buyer can repeat what you sell in one sentence.
done_looks_like: A single sentence: "I help {buyer} do {outcome} in {timeframe} for {price}."
deliverable_prompt: Draft 3 variants of a one-line productized offer for the founder using their buyer_segment, outcome, and price. Return the tightest one first.

title: Post one CTA to your audience
why_now_template: You have an audience but have never asked them to buy. One direct CTA post today.
done_looks_like: One post published with a clear ask + how to reply.
deliverable_prompt: Draft an audience-facing post that describes the offer and invites replies from anyone who wants it.

title: Send 10 targeted cold DMs
why_now_template: No warm network available for this buyer. Cold outreach is the path — but only with a specific hook per person.
done_looks_like: 10 personalized cold DMs sent. Not a template blast.
deliverable_prompt: Draft the outreach frame + 10 personalized cold DMs for this buyer segment. Each DM must reference something specific about the recipient.

title: Post a value comment in 3 communities
why_now_template: No audience, no warm net. Communities where your buyer already hangs out are the shortest path to a first conversation.
done_looks_like: 3 substantive answers/comments posted in relevant communities.
deliverable_prompt: Identify 3 communities where the buyer segment is active, draft one substantive value-first comment/answer for each.

title: Ask 3 people for one intro each
why_now_template: Referrals convert 3x cold. Ask the 3 most-connected people you know for one specific intro each.
done_looks_like: 3 referral asks sent. Each names the buyer type explicitly.
deliverable_prompt: Draft 3 personalized referral-ask messages, each one specifying the exact buyer type and why an intro would help.

title: Ask the 3 strongest-fit reachable contacts today
why_now_template: You already have reachable buyers or past clients. The next revenue move is a direct ask, not another preparation step.
done_looks_like: 3 direct-ask messages sent to the 3 strongest-fit reachable contacts before closing TrueBlazer.
deliverable_prompt: Write a direct-ask message the founder can send today to 3 strongest-fit reachable contacts they choose (past clients, warm connections, or referrers). Do not invent names, companies, or prior interactions — reference only what the founder can plausibly recall. Anchor on the buyer segment and the productized offer. 90-120 words, direct, no "leverage", no "great job", one clear ask (a 15-minute conversation or a yes/no on the offer).

title: Send 5 warm DMs today
why_now_template: Warm network + no outreach = leaving revenue on the floor. 5 messages, personal, no pitch.
done_looks_like: 5 DMs sent to warm-network fits. Reply, not pitch.
deliverable_prompt: Draft 5 personalized warm DMs opening a conversation (no pitch) for the founder to send to warm-network buyers.

title: Run the winning motion again on the winning channel
why_now_template: You already know one motion worked. Repeat it before experimenting.
done_looks_like: The same message/motion that produced the sale sent to at least 10 lookalike prospects on the same channel this week.
deliverable_prompt: Instruct the founder to replicate the exact outreach motion that produced their first sale — same channel (from the revenue event source_channel if present, otherwise the winning conversation's channel), same hook, same offer framing. Do not invent prior message text; reference "the outreach message that led to your first sale" and ask the founder to reuse it against 10 lookalike prospects this week. Add one line on tracking: log each new conversation to see if reply-rate matches the winning baseline.

title: Build a 10-name lookalike list of the winning buyer
why_now_template: The fastest path to a second sale is finding more of the buyer who just paid you.
done_looks_like: 10 named prospects added to the buyer list who match the winning buyer's segment, size, and channel.
deliverable_prompt: Guide the founder to build a 10-name lookalike list of the buyer who just paid. Reference the winning buyer's segment (from money_paths.buyer_segment) and the source_channel of the revenue event. Do not invent specific company names or contacts. Provide search cues: role titles, company size, industry, where to look on the winning channel, and what qualification signal proves fit before adding.

title: Teardown the win — what actually worked
why_now_template: One sale is evidence worth repeating. Before scaling, capture what worked so it can be reproduced.
done_looks_like: A 6-field win teardown captured: buyer traits, channel, hook, timing, price, decision driver.
deliverable_prompt: Prompt the founder through a 15-minute structured teardown of the sale they just closed. Reference only what the revenue event and the winning buyer conversation contain — do not invent buyer names or quotes. Ask about: who the buyer was (traits and segment fit), which channel produced first contact, the specific hook or message that got a reply, timing/trigger, price and scope, and the one thing that made them say yes. Output as 6 short prompts the founder answers into TrueBlazer.

title: Switch outreach channel
why_now_template: Your buyers are not on the channel you are pushing. Try one different channel today.
done_looks_like: 5 messages sent on a new channel to the same buyer type.
deliverable_prompt: Recommend an alternate channel for this buyer segment given they have not replied on the current channel. Give 3 concrete steps to send 5 messages there today.

title: Send a 60-second personal video
why_now_template: Video replies convert dramatically higher than text for high-touch offers. Send 3 today.
done_looks_like: 3 personalized video DMs sent.
deliverable_prompt: Write the 60-second script + shot list for 3 personalized founder video DMs to warm-ish prospects.

title: Rewrite your opener with a new hook
why_now_template: You sent messages, zero replies. The hook is wrong. Change the first sentence, keep the offer.
done_looks_like: A new opener + 5 test sends using it.
deliverable_prompt: Analyze what the founder has been sending (assume generic), and rewrite the first 2 sentences with a specific, curiosity-inducing hook.
